origin_name: Salaya, near Vadinar, Jamnagar district, GUJARAT
notes: Evidence: 'The 2663 km long crude oil pipeline with an installed capacity of 25 MMTPA originates from Salaya near Vadinar in Jamnagar district on the coast of Gujarat to bring crude oil to IndianOil's Refineries at Koyali in Gujarat, Mathura in Uttar Pradesh and Panipat in Haryana.' Establishes: a single crude trunk line from the Gujarat coast serving three IndianOil refineries; destination_name records the name-bearing terminus only and the full refinery set is expressed as edges in network_links.csv. The marine origin 'Salaya' is NOT the same entity as PORT002 Vadinar Offshore Oil Terminal and no port endpoint is asserted - see docs/data_sources.md. commissioned_date is null: not stated by the operator page. The operator page carries no publication date, so report_date is set equal to retrieved_at. The same page further states 'Two Single Point Mooring (SPM) systems are operated at Vadinar to unload the crude oil received from tankers including Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) with offshore pipelines of 25 km' and 'At Vadinar, IndianOil has a vast crude oil tank farm having 18 tanks with a total capacity of 1.5 MMT', which places this line's marine intake facilities at Vadinar under IndianOil operation. That still does not resolve a port endpoint: MoPNG-PS&W records three Single Buoy Moorings at Vadinar under Deendayal Port Authority (PORT002) while IndianOil records two SPM systems of its own, and no source reconciles the two counts or states that IndianOil's SPM systems are Deendayal facilities. PHASE 2 STEP 4 (2026-08-23): Deendayal Port Authority's own 'Off-shore Oil Terminal (OOT) - Vadinar' page (https://www.deendayalport.gov.in/en/about-us/off-shore-oil-terminal-oot-vadinar/) was sought as the most direct possible reconciling source; every retrieval attempt returned the site's own application error page ('Something went wrong. You will be redirected to the home page') with no substantive content, and no Wayback Machine snapshot of that URL exists. A Tariff Authority for Major Ports order concerning the Vadinar Off-Shore Oil Terminal (https://tariffauthority.gov.in/writereaddata/UploadFile/DPTG260ORDRPASD08062018ORDRALL_1092.pdf) could not be retrieved at all on repeated attempts (connection failure). Both are recorded here as failed retrievals, not as evidence. IndianOil's own crude-oil-pipelines page was re-read in full and names no port authority anywhere in connection with Vadinar. No authoritative source reconciling the SBM/SPM counts was located. STATUS: PARTIALLY RESOLVED - the marine intake's location and operator (Vadinar, IndianOil, two SPM systems) are established; the specific port record those facilities correspond to is not, and no port endpoint is created for PL001.

operator: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (for Bharat Oman Refineries Limited)
source: BPCL - Vadinar Bina Pipeline Fully Commissioned
notes: Evidence: the operator's own announcement records the '935 km long, 24 inch diameter Vadinar-Bina crude oil pipeline' as 'fully commissioned' on 6 June 2010, from Vadinar in Gujarat to the BORL refinery at Bina in Madhya Pradesh, with pumping stations at Thamna and Bawdi and intermediate stations at Somasar and Sandavata. Establishes: operator, length, both termini, design capacity 6 MMTPA and commissioning date. report_date is the commissioning date the announcement is effective for; the page itself carries no publication date. The marine origin at Vadinar is NOT resolved to any port_id - Gujarat Maritime Board's captive-jetty register places the BORL crude SPM at Sikka while this announcement names Vadinar, and that conflict is unresolved, so no port endpoint is asserted. BORL's own pre-feasibility report, filed on the Government of India environmental clearance portal, records the same system in more detail: BORL is 'operating a 6.0 MMTPA Refinery at Bina in Madhya Pradesh, with a Crude Oil Terminal at Vadinar in the Gulf of Kachchh', its CALM-type Single Point Mooring buoy 'is located at Lat. 22o 33' 44'' N, Long. 69o 45' 38'' E, about 7 km offshore from the Vadinar coast', and 'The crude oil is pumped from the Crude Oil Tanks through a 943 km long pipeline to Bina'. Two lengths for the same line are therefore on record - 935 km in the BPCL commissioning announcement and 943 km in the BORL filing. length_km keeps the 935 km commissioning figure and the other is preserved here; neither was averaged. BORL publishes exactly one SPM and the Gujarat Maritime Board captive-jetty register lists exactly one 'BORL - SPM', so the two publishers describe one facility under two different locality labels, Vadinar and Sikka. That label conflict is unresolved and no port endpoint is asserted. PHASE 2 STEP 4 (2026-08-23): searched Gujarat Maritime Board, Tariff Authority for Major Ports, BORL/BPCL and MoEFCC sources again for a document naming this facility under one locality label together with coordinates, operator and terminal name. None was found. gmbports.org has no 'Vadinar' port page at all (confirmed HTTP 404 on direct retrieval); the board's only Kachchh-area crude entry for this facility remains the captive-jetty register's 'BORL - SPM  Sikka  Crude oil' line already on record, so the label conflict with the BORL/BPCL Vadinar naming stands unreconciled. STATUS: PARTIALLY RESOLVED - the operational relationship (BORL's single SPM feeding its Bina refinery through the Vadinar-named Crude Oil Terminal) is established; the specific port record for that terminal is not, and no port endpoint is created for PL005.
